significance.justification: Verified true, the claim would establish both a form-(iii) behavioral relation—"gap rate ... rises with procedure complexity"—and a form-(ii) causal decomposition in which "declarative description" and the "executable pathway" are weakly coupled, with steering the latter repairing execution without changing recitation. The phenomenon would constrain when correctly stated procedures predict actual behavior, while the mechanism would explain the mismatch and directly qualify explanation-faithfulness assumptions examined by Turpin et al. (2023) and Lanham et al. (2023); unlike the median direction-plus-repair claim, it separates two readouts and predicts their divergence across complexity. Verified false under the stated alternatives would distinguish a shared-competence account from the proposed dissociation, although failure of patching alone would not rule out every possible dissociation mechanism; true and false therefore denote meaningfully different states of the world. Topic substitution fails: merely restating that knowledge retrieval can fail would not earn this score, because the added complexity relation and recitation/execution causal decomposition are what support it.

reach.justification: The principal handle is the intervention "steering the execution circuit toward the recited-rule direction," accompanied by a recitation-execution gap diagnostic; the steering is ex ante because it acts during intermediate computation before the executed output, whereas measuring the gap itself is largely post hoc. After per-model re-extraction, the causal direction may have to be rediscovered, but the claimed relation that gaps increase with procedure complexity still predicts which procedure classes should be riskier, so some substantive content survives recalibration. The asserted scope covers "string/morphology rules, list operations, modular and base-conversion arithmetic, [and] rule-following games," and the stated downstream users include instruction-following auditors and builders of "tool invocation" and "agentic workflows," not only researchers analyzing the representation. Topic substitution fails: the broad knowledge-retrieval topic alone supplies neither this before-output intervention nor the complexity-linked diagnostic, so the score rests on claim-specific handles.
